questions.stem: What is the definition of half-life?

options.text: The time taken for the radiation to become safe
The time taken for half the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay
The time taken for all the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay
Half the time it takes for a radioactive source to fully decay

questions.explanation: Half-life is the time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay, or equivalently, the time for the activity (count rate) to halve.

questions.stem: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 6 hours and an initial activity of 800 Bq. What is the activity after 18 hours?
questions.explanation: 18 hours = 3 half-lives (18 / 6 = 3). After each half-life the activity halves: 800 -> 400 -> 200 -> 100 Bq. So after 3 half-lives, the activity is 100 Bq.

questions.stem: Which of the following can change the half-life of a radioactive isotope?

options.text: Nothing can change it; half-life is a fixed property of each isotope

questions.explanation: Half-life is a constant property of each radioactive isotope. It cannot be changed by temperature, pressure, chemical reactions, or any other physical or chemical means.

questions.stem: What is the unit of radioactive activity?
questions.explanation: Activity is measured in becquerels (Bq). One becquerel equals one decay per second. It measures the rate at which a radioactive source is decaying.

questions.stem: A sample starts with 1000 undecayed nuclei. After 2 half-lives, how many undecayed nuclei remain?
questions.explanation: After 1 half-life: 1000 / 2 = 500. After 2 half-lives: 500 / 2 = 250 undecayed nuclei remain. Each half-life halves the number of remaining radioactive nuclei.

questions.stem: Why does the activity of a radioactive sample decrease over time?

options.text: Because the half-life gets longer over time
Because fewer undecayed nuclei remain, so fewer decays happen per second

questions.explanation: As nuclei decay, there are fewer undecayed nuclei left. Since each nucleus has the same probability of decaying, fewer nuclei means fewer decays per second, so the activity decreases.

questions.stem: Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years. Why is it useful for dating ancient objects?

options.text: Because its long half-life means measurable amounts remain in objects thousands of years old
Because it emits gamma rays that can be easily detected
Because it is found in all metals

questions.explanation: Carbon-14's half-life of 5730 years is long enough that detectable amounts remain in organic materials up to about 50,000 years old, allowing the age of ancient artefacts and fossils to be estimated.
